lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Somewhere in the Pacific, one whale sings at a pitch no known whale uses.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Blue whales call between ten and thirty-nine.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: The microphones that caught it were Navy hydrophones, laid on the seabed to hunt Soviet submarines.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: And nobody has ever seen the animal.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: When the Navy opened its recordings, Woods Hole ocean scientists followed that voice for twelve years.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Every autumn it swam from the Aleutian Islands to California, alone, following no other whales.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: On the seventh of December, a Navy technician watched the trace climb on the screen, far above every other whale.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Over the years its voice deepened, slightly, like an animal growing up.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Then, in twenty ten, sensors off California heard the same strange song in two places at once.
